extraction.body: Wells Fargo is reportedly discussing a crypto-trading-liquidity arrangement with Payward, the parent company behind Kraken. The talks offer a view into how a large bank could reach digital-asset markets without operating an exchange or building every part of the trading system itself. CoinDesk reported that Wells Fargo and Payward are discussing crypto-trading liquidity . Neither company has announced an agreement, launch date, product scope or eligible clients. CoinDesk reported that the discussions could involve Payward supplying liquidity for crypto trading. In practical terms, liquidity is the pool of buyers and sellers available when a customer wants to trade. Deeper liquidity makes it easier to complete a large order quickly without pushing the price far from the market level shown on screen. That becomes especially important when a bank serves wealthy clients, companies or institutions that may want to trade more than a small retail order. A polished app and a recognised banking brand do not by themselves guarantee competitive execution. The bank also needs access to prices, counterparties and trading systems that can handle an order when it arrives. Payward has been building services around that part of the market. Its public materials describe a business that extends beyond the Kraken exchange, covering trading, custody, payments, lending and institutional infrastructure. Payward’s website lists Kraken Prime among its banking products, alongside services designed for professional market participants. Payward already has a public example of how such a relationship can work. In an October 5 announcement, Singapore Gulf Bank said it would use Kraken Prime as an additional source of digital-asset liquidity and draw on Payward’s markets to price trades for its customers. The Payward-Singapore Gulf Bank partnership also links that market access to round-the-clock settlement through the bank’s clearing network. A client can move funds into the trading environment outside the usual banking cut-off times, while the specialist provider contributes pricing and access to crypto markets. That arrangement does not reveal the terms under discussion with Wells Fargo. It does, however, show the type of infrastructure Payward is publicly offering to regulated banks: a connection between traditional customer accounts and a crypto trading venue with established market access. “Crypto trading” can describe a number of different functions. The party that owns the client relationship may not be the party executing the trade, holding the assets or settling the transaction. Separating those jobs lets a bank add a crypto service while relying on a specialist provider where it lacks its own market infrastructure. CoinDesk’s report does not say which of these functions could form part of a Wells Fargo arrangement. That distinction would shape the customer experience, the regulatory obligations and the risks each company takes on. If a bank offers clients a way to buy or sell crypto, the cost of execution quickly becomes visible through the final price. A wide spread, delayed fill or limited access during volatile periods can make the service less useful, even when the bank has handled onboarding and compliance well. Working with a large liquidity provider can address some of those problems, but it also creates dependence on the provider’s markets, technology and risk controls. The service needs clear rules for pricing, outages, withdrawals, settlement timing and the treatment of client assets. Those details often matter more to users than the announcement of a new trading option. The reported talks do not establish that Wells Fargo has launched a crypto-trading service. They point instead to a route banks may use as digital-asset markets mature: keep the customer relationship and bank controls in-house, while connecting to specialist firms for the market access that is harder to build alone. passages: Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, is in talks to become a crypto liquidity provider to U.S. financial giant Wells Fargo (WFC), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter.
Payward is separately in talks with custody banking giant BNY over a broad financial-infrastructure partnership, CoinDesk reported last week.
Those discussions could cover crypto products, custody, wealth management, trading and payments, further extending the company’s ties with established financial institutions.
Beyond operating Kraken, Payward offers trading, payments and financial infrastructure spanning spot crypto, derivatives, tokenized equities, custody, staking and traditional securities.
Its Payward Services division provides infrastructure to banks, fintechs, brokerages and payment companies.
Payward and Wells Fargo both declined to comment.
Wells Fargo already offers spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) to eligible wealth clients and has backed crypto compliance firm Elliptic and trading technology provider Talos.
It has also announced plans for blockchain-based deposits and joined a consortium developing a dollar stablecoin, extending its digital asset activities into payments.
Crypto exchanges often serve as gateways to digital asset liquidity for banks and institutional investors, providing access to trading venues and helping execute orders.

For example, Coinbase Prime aggregates liquidity across multiple markets, while Kraken offers banks technology to integrate crypto trading into their own platforms, allowing them to serve clients without building the infrastructure themselves
Under the potential deal, Wyoming-based Payward would supply liquidity for trading in crypto assets, the people said, speaking on condition of anonymity because the matter is private.
The discussions suggest major banks are increasingly turning to established crypto companies to support their digital asset ambitions.
A friendlier U.S. regulatory environment is also helping drive that shift.
The California-based financial services firm strengthened its digital assets team earlier this year by hiring former Citi (C) banker Mark Gracia.

The bank also served as Nasdaq’s exclusive capital markets adviser on the exchange operator’s September agreement to invest $100 million in Payward and deepen their collaboration on tokenized equities and market surveillance.

extraction.body: Robinhood has made its first proprietary Bitcoin purchase, putting approximately $25 million of company money into BTC — crossing a threshold that separates platforms that merely facilitate Bitcoin trading from companies that actually hold it. He framed the purchase as conviction, not capital reallocation — "it represents how deeply we care about bitcoin and the ecosystem around it" — and was direct about the scale relative to the company: "Robinhood is a massive company at this point, with a market cap in the $100 billion range. So the $25 million worth of bitcoin is not going to change a lot of the current trajectory of the company."The gap between the $25 million purchase and the $100 billion valuation is deliberate. Robinhood had 27.4 million funded customers and held $307 billion in platform assets as of Q1 2026. A $25 million BTC position is 0.025% of its market cap. The posture is.As recently as November 2025, at Robinhood's third-quarter earnings call, incoming CFO Shiv Verma said the company was "still thinking about" the move, weighing the community-alignment benefit against the cost of tying up capital, and raising the question of whether adding Bitcoin to the balance sheet makes any decision for shareholders who can already buy BTC directly through the Robinhood platform. That deliberation about Bitcoin treasury has now closed.What Changed — and Why It Required an Accounting Rule to Change FirstRobinhood did not buy Bitcoin in 2024 or early 2025 even as corporate BTC adoption accelerated around it. The accounting environment is part of the reason. Under the old US GAAP model for crypto assets, companies could only write down Bitcoin holdings when prices fell — but could never recognize gains when prices rose. A corporate Bitcoin position in 2023 created asymmetric accounting punishment: losses hit the income statement, gains were invisible until the asset was sold. That model made holding BTC on an operating company's books artificially punitive.That changed with FASB Accounting Standards Update 2023-08, issued December 13, 2023 and effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2024. Under ASU 2023-08, in-scope crypto assets — Bitcoin included — must be measured at fair value at every reporting date, with gains and losses flowing through net income each quarter. Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), which had already adopted the standard early, described it in its Q1 2025 filing as likely to "have a material impact on our financial results, increase the volatility of our financial results and affect the carrying value of our bitcoin on our balance sheet."The ASU 2023-08 fair-value rule removed the structural disincentive for operating companies to hold BTC. Robinhood's first balance sheet purchase came roughly nine months after the rule took effect for most companies.What a HOOD Shareholder Actually FacesHere is the structural consequence the headline dollar amount does not fully communicate.Robinhood's revenue is already substantially correlated with Bitcoin prices. In Q4 2024, crypto trading accounted for 53% of Robinhood's transaction-based revenue — then fell to 12.88% in Q2 2026 when Bitcoin's price declined. When BTC drops, Robinhood's trading volumes compress and its crypto transaction revenue contracts. This has been true since the company launched crypto trading.What is new is that the $25 million corporate Bitcoin position is now marked to market every quarter under ASU 2023-08. When Bitcoin prices fall, Robinhood's quarterly earnings will now reflect unrealized losses on its corporate BTC holding — in addition to the revenue contraction from lower trading volumes. When prices rise, the reverse applies, but the point stands structurally: HOOD shareholders face Bitcoin price exposure on two separate lines of the income statement simultaneously, and neither exposure hedges the other.This makes Robinhood's position categorically different from both ends of the corporate Bitcoin spectrum. Strategy (the company formerly known as MicroStrategy), which holds approximately 848,000 BTC as of early October 2026 — roughly 69% of all Bitcoin owned by listed companies — is a leveraged BTC pure-play; its equity is designed to move with Bitcoin, and shareholders self-select for that risk. Robinhood sits in a new category: an operating company whose revenue is already Bitcoin-correlated and whose balance sheet is now also Bitcoin-marked-to-market."Cryptocurrencies' high volatility and uncertain regulatory landscape are misaligned with the fundamental goals of treasury management — stability, liquidity, and capital preservation," David Krause, a finance professor at Marquette University, noted in a January 2026 research publication on corporate Bitcoin holdings. Standard Chartered's Global Head of Digital Assets Research, Geoffrey Kendrick, has raised related concerns about the broader corporate treasury trend, warning that "Bitcoin treasuries are adding to Bitcoin buying pressure for now, but we see a risk that this may reverse over time."Neither warning is directed at Robinhood specifically. But both apply with particular force to an operating company that already earns substantially from Bitcoin trading activity.Custody vs. Corporate: Why the Numbers Look ConfusingRobinhood controls approximately $25 billion in crypto assets across approximately 1.7 million wallet addresses on 12 different blockchains. A post circulating on social media before Wednesday's DAS Asia disclosure cited this figure and claimed Robinhood was a massive Bitcoin holder. Those $25 billion in crypto assets spread across Robinhood's customer custody wallets belong entirely to Robinhood's customers — Robinhood holds the private keys, but the coins are not on Robinhood's own books.The $25 million corporate BTC purchase is a different category. It sits on Robinhood's own balance sheet, subject to FASB ASU 2023-08 quarterly fair-value measurement. The distinction matters for both accounting and risk: customer custody creates zero direct P&L exposure for Robinhood (it earns custody-related revenue from fees and services, not from BTC price movements). The corporate position creates direct earnings exposure every quarter.Bitcoin was trading near $83,360 at the time of the DAS Asia disclosure, per CoinDesk market data.Robinhood's Position in the Corporate Bitcoin LandscapeWith the purchase, Robinhood joins a cohort that has expanded dramatically since Strategy made its initial $250 million BTC purchase in August 2020. More than 170 publicly traded companies worldwide now hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets, with combined corporate holdings exceeding 1.2 million BTC — representing more than 6% of Bitcoin's hard-capped supply of 21 million coins.Strategy remains the dominant holder by orders of magnitude. At approximately 848,000 BTC, it accounts for roughly 69% of all corporate-held Bitcoin globally. MARA Holdings and other Bitcoin miners hold substantial secondary positions. Among traditional, non-Bitcoin-native operating companies, Robinhood joins Tesla and Block (the payments company founded by Jack Dorsey) in what analysts describe as symbolic or diversification allocations rather than primary treasury strategies.The corporate treasury trend has also been bolstered by the FASB accounting shift. More than 140 publicly traded companies had adopted Bitcoin treasury positions in the first quarter of 2026 alone, with corporate treasuries collectively adding roughly 62,000 BTC in that quarter.Robinhood has not disclosed a formal BTC accumulation policy, and Kerbrat's language — emphasizing conviction over capital deployment — signals the company is not attempting to replicate Strategy's leveraged, all-in approach.Why Robinhood Chain Makes This More Than SymbolicRobinhood's Bitcoin balance sheet purchase did not arrive in isolation. It follows 98 days after Robinhood Chain — the company's permissionless Ethereum Layer 2 network built on Arbitrum's Orbit stack — went live on mainnet on July 1, 2026. The chain carries chain ID 4663, processes transactions off the Ethereum mainchain in rollup batches before settling back to Ethereum for security, and uses ETH as its native gas token.Since its mainnet debut, Robinhood Chain has added tokenized stock and ETF products (Stock Tokens), a US dollar stablecoin (USDG), and a yield-bearing lending product called Robinhood Earn.

A $25 million BTC position is 0.025% of its market cap.

The posture is.As recently as November 2025, at Robinhood's third-quarter earnings call, incoming CFO Shiv Verma said the company was "still thinking about" the move, weighing the community-alignment benefit against the cost of tying up capital, and raising the question of whether adding Bitcoin to the balance sheet makes any decision for shareholders who can already buy BTC directly through the Robinhood platform.

That deliberation about Bitcoin treasury has now closed.What Changed — and Why It Required an Accounting Rule to Change FirstRobinhood did not buy Bitcoin in 2024 or early 2025 even as corporate BTC adoption accelerated around it.
The accounting environment is part of the reason.
Under the old US GAAP model for crypto assets, companies could only write down Bitcoin holdings when prices fell — but could never recognize gains when prices rose.
A corporate Bitcoin position in 2023 created asymmetric accounting punishment: losses hit the income statement, gains were invisible until the asset was sold.

That model made holding BTC on an operating company's books artificially punitive.That changed with FASB Accounting Standards Update 2023-08, issued December 13, 2023 and effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2024.
Under ASU 2023-08, in-scope crypto assets — Bitcoin included — must be measured at fair value at every reporting date, with gains and losses flowing through net income each quarter.

Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), which had already adopted the standard early, described it in its Q1 2025 filing as likely to "have a material impact on our financial results, increase the volatility of our financial results and affect the carrying value of our bitcoin on our balance sheet."The ASU 2023-08 fair-value rule removed the structural disincentive for operating companies to hold BTC.

Robinhood's first balance sheet purchase came roughly nine months after the rule took effect for most companies.What a HOOD Shareholder Actually FacesHere is the structural consequence the headline dollar amount does not fully communicate.Robinhood's revenue is already substantially correlated with Bitcoin prices.
In Q4 2024, crypto trading accounted for 53% of Robinhood's transaction-based revenue — then fell to 12.88% in Q2 2026 when Bitcoin's price declined.
When BTC drops, Robinhood's trading volumes compress and its crypto transaction revenue contracts.
This has been true since the company launched crypto trading.What is new is that the $25 million corporate Bitcoin position is now marked to market every quarter under ASU 2023-08.
When Bitcoin prices fall, Robinhood's quarterly earnings will now reflect unrealized losses on its corporate BTC holding — in addition to the revenue contraction from lower trading volumes.

When prices rise, the reverse applies, but the point stands structurally: HOOD shareholders face Bitcoin price exposure on two separate lines of the income statement simultaneously, and neither exposure hedges the other.This makes Robinhood's position categorically different from both ends of the corporate Bitcoin spectrum.

Strategy (the company formerly known as MicroStrategy), which holds approximately 848,000 BTC as of early October 2026 — roughly 69% of all Bitcoin owned by listed companies — is a leveraged BTC pure-play; its equity is designed to move with Bitcoin, and shareholders self-select for that risk.

Robinhood sits in a new category: an operating company whose revenue is already Bitcoin-correlated and whose balance sheet is now also Bitcoin-marked-to-market."Cryptocurrencies' high volatility and uncertain regulatory landscape are misaligned with the fundamental goals of treasury management — stability, liquidity, and capital preservation," David Krause, a finance professor at Marquette University, noted in a January 2026 research publication on corporate Bitcoin holdings.

Standard Chartered's Global Head of Digital Assets Research, Geoffrey Kendrick, has raised related concerns about the broader corporate treasury trend, warning that "Bitcoin treasuries are adding to Bitcoin buying pressure for now, but we see a risk that this may reverse over time."Neither warning is directed at Robinhood specifically.
But both apply with particular force to an operating company that already earns substantially from Bitcoin trading activity.Custody vs.
Corporate: Why the Numbers Look ConfusingRobinhood controls approximately $25 billion in crypto assets across approximately 1.7 million wallet addresses on 12 different blockchains.
A post circulating on social media before Wednesday's DAS Asia disclosure cited this figure and claimed Robinhood was a massive Bitcoin holder.

Those $25 billion in crypto assets spread across Robinhood's customer custody wallets belong entirely to Robinhood's customers — Robinhood holds the private keys, but the coins are not on Robinhood's own books.The $25 million corporate BTC purchase is a different category.
It sits on Robinhood's own balance sheet, subject to FASB ASU 2023-08 quarterly fair-value measurement.

The distinction matters for both accounting and risk: customer custody creates zero direct P&L exposure for Robinhood (it earns custody-related revenue from fees and services, not from BTC price movements).

The corporate position creates direct earnings exposure every quarter.Bitcoin was trading near $83,360 at the time of the DAS Asia disclosure, per CoinDesk market data.Robinhood's Position in the Corporate Bitcoin LandscapeWith the purchase, Robinhood joins a cohort that has expanded dramatically since Strategy made its initial $250 million BTC purchase in August 2020.

More than 170 publicly traded companies worldwide now hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets, with combined corporate holdings exceeding 1.2 million BTC — representing more than 6% of Bitcoin's hard-capped supply of 21 million coins.Strategy remains the dominant holder by orders of magnitude.
At approximately 848,000 BTC, it accounts for roughly 69% of all corporate-held Bitcoin globally.
MARA Holdings and other Bitcoin miners hold substantial secondary positions.

Among traditional, non-Bitcoin-native operating companies, Robinhood joins Tesla and Block (the payments company founded by Jack Dorsey) in what analysts describe as symbolic or diversification allocations rather than primary treasury strategies.The corporate treasury trend has also been bolstered by the FASB accounting shift.

More than 140 publicly traded companies had adopted Bitcoin treasury positions in the first quarter of 2026 alone, with corporate treasuries collectively adding roughly 62,000 BTC in that quarter.Robinhood has not disclosed a formal BTC accumulation policy, and Kerbrat's language — emphasizing conviction over capital deployment — signals the company is not attempting to replicate Strategy's leveraged, all-in approach.Why Robinhood Chain Makes This More Than SymbolicRobinhood's Bitcoin balance sheet purchase did not arrive in isolation.
It follows 98 days after Robinhood Chain — the company's permissionless Ethereum Layer 2 network built on Arbitrum's Orbit stack — went live on mainnet on July 1, 2026.

The chain carries chain ID 4663, processes transactions off the Ethereum mainchain in rollup batches before settling back to Ethereum for security, and uses ETH as its native gas token.Since its mainnet debut, Robinhood Chain has added tokenized stock and ETF products (Stock Tokens), a US dollar stablecoin (USDG), and a yield-bearing lending product called Robinhood Earn.

Bitcoin traded near $84,000 at the time of the disclosure, having closed around $85,540 on Oct.
The move marks a shift in tone from the company's posture just under a year ago, when executives had expressed caution about holding volatile crypto assets on the corporate books.

Together, those firms and others account for well over 1.2 million bitcoin on their balance sheets.

extraction.body: Robinhood has taken a direct stake in bitcoin, adding roughly $25 million of the cryptocurrency to its corporate balance sheet and joining a growing list of public companies treating the token as a treasury asset rather than merely a product for customers. The purchase was disclosed Wednesday by Johann Kerbrat, Robinhood's senior vice president and general manager of crypto and international, during an interview with The Block's Starting Block program at the Digital Asset Summit Asia conference in Singapore. The company has not separately confirmed the transaction through a press release or regulatory filing. "We care deeply about bitcoin and the ecosystem around it," Kerbrat said. "For us, it's more aligning our company and our vision with the crypto community." The executive was careful to frame the allocation as a strategic signal rather than a financial bet that would reshape the company's trajectory. With Robinhood's market capitalization hovering around $100 billion, he noted, a $25 million bitcoin position "is not going to change a lot of the current trajectory of the company." The move marks a shift in tone from the company's posture just under a year ago, when executives had expressed caution about holding volatile crypto assets on the corporate books. Robinhood has for years facilitated customer trading in digital tokens, but those holdings are segregated from company treasury assets and do not expose the firm to bitcoin's price swings. The new allocation changes that dynamic, giving Robinhood direct exposure to the cryptocurrency's market value. Robinhood now stands alongside more than 170 publicly traded companies worldwide that hold bitcoin as a corporate asset, a trend that Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR) initiated in 2020 when it began converting cash reserves into the cryptocurrency. Current corporate holders include Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA), Block (NYSE:XYZ), MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA), CleanSpark (NASDAQ:CLSK) and Riot Platforms (NASDAQ:RIOT). Together, those firms and others account for well over 1.2 million bitcoin on their balance sheets. Strategy continues to add to its position. The company disclosed this week that it purchased an additional 334 bitcoin between Sept. 28 and Oct. 4 for roughly $28.7 million, at an average price of $85,838.80 per coin. That brings its total holdings to 848,000 bitcoin, far eclipsing any other corporate treasury. Robinhood's $25 million allocation is modest by comparison, but it carries outsized symbolic weight given the brokerage's visibility among retail investors and its more than 28 million funded customers globally. The company has been methodically expanding its crypto footprint beyond simple spot trading. In July, it launched Robinhood Chain, an Ethereum-compatible Layer 2 network built on Arbitrum and designed for tokenized real-world assets and decentralized finance. Since the mainnet went live, the chain has rolled out tokenized stock products, a stablecoin called USDG, and yield-bearing lending through Robinhood Earn, while integrating DeFi protocols such as Uniswap and infrastructure from Chainlink, Alchemy and BitGo. The network has already reached $1.05 billion in total value locked, according to earlier reporting. Kerbrat said trading volume for stock tokens on the chain has grown to the point where it is approaching limits set by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's innovation exemption for tokenized U.S. equities. Robinhood has also signaled plans to launch perpetual futures trading for eligible U.S. customers, covering eight assets. Chief Executive Officer Vlad Tenev has described the offering as "America's first true perps," with no expiry and profit and loss settled every 15 minutes. The company reported 28.6 million funded customers and $384 billion in total platform assets for August. Crypto notional trading volume reached $17.5 billion during that month, underscoring why the bitcoin treasury position is viewed more as an alignment of corporate identity with the asset class than as a meaningful capital allocation. Bitcoin traded near $84,000 at the time of the disclosure, having closed around $85,540 on Oct. 6. The cryptocurrency has remained below recent local highs, and a $25 million purchase is unlikely to move its price in any meaningful way given the asset's overall market size. Robinhood shares were down roughly 3% in premarket trading, extending a pullback from a recent high of $125. The stock has broken below its 20-day exponential moving average at $114 and is testing the 50-day exponential moving average near $109, with the relative strength index at 48.75 indicating fading momentum. The shares still hold above the 100-day and 200-day exponential moving averages, suggesting the longer-term uptrend remains intact. For investors, the more significant implication lies in signaling. A consumer-facing brokerage with millions of users formalizing a direct bitcoin position reinforces the narrative that the cryptocurrency is becoming a standard corporate treasury consideration, particularly for companies with crypto-adjacent business lines. It also invites scrutiny of how such holdings will be valued and disclosed in future financial reporting. Robinhood has not detailed a long-term target size for its bitcoin holdings, nor has it indicated whether additional allocations or other digital assets might follow. The company's press team did not immediately respond to inquiries about potential future purchases. The disclosure arrives amid continued competition among brokerages, exchanges and fintech platforms to capture crypto-focused customers. Firms are increasingly differentiating themselves not just through trading fees, but through the depth of their underlying commitment to digital assets. Robinhood's balance sheet purchase adds another data point to that competitive landscape, one that suggests the company sees its own treasury as another venue for demonstrating conviction in the asset class it increasingly serves. coreStoryFacts.text: Robinhood has added approximately $25 million worth of bitcoin to its corporate balance sheet, marking a significant step in its growing involvement in cryptocurrency.
This move, confirmed by Robinhood's senior VP Johann Kerbrat, reflects the company's deep commitment to bitcoin and the crypto ecosystem.
Robinhood continues to expand its crypto offerings, including launching an Ethereum-compatible network and tokenized stock products, indicating ongoing growth in its crypto business.

The posture is.As recently as November 2025, at Robinhood's third-quarter earnings call, incoming CFO Shiv Verma said the company was "still thinking about" the move, weighing the community-alignment benefit against the cost of tying up capital, and raising the question of whether adding Bitcoin to the balance sheet makes any decision for shareholders who can already buy BTC directly through the Robinhood platform.

Robinhood's first balance sheet purchase came roughly nine months after the rule took effect for most companies.What a HOOD Shareholder Actually FacesHere is the structural consequence the headline dollar amount does not fully communicate.Robinhood's revenue is already substantially correlated with Bitcoin prices.

More than 140 publicly traded companies had adopted Bitcoin treasury positions in the first quarter of 2026 alone, with corporate treasuries collectively adding roughly 62,000 BTC in that quarter.Robinhood has not disclosed a formal BTC accumulation policy, and Kerbrat's language — emphasizing conviction over capital deployment — signals the company is not attempting to replicate Strategy's leveraged, all-in approach.Why Robinhood Chain Makes This More Than SymbolicRobinhood's Bitcoin balance sheet purchase did not arrive in isolation.

Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), which had already adopted the standard early, described it in its Q1 2025 filing as likely to "have a material impact on our financial results, increase the volatility of our financial results and affect the carrying value of our bitcoin on our balance sheet."The ASU 2023-08 fair-value rule removed the structural disincentive for operating companies to hold BTC.

When prices rise, the reverse applies, but the point stands structurally: HOOD shareholders face Bitcoin price exposure on two separate lines of the income statement simultaneously, and neither exposure hedges the other.This makes Robinhood's position categorically different from both ends of the corporate Bitcoin spectrum.
In Q4 2024, crypto trading accounted for 53% of Robinhood's transaction-based revenue — then fell to 12.88% in Q2 2026 when Bitcoin's price declined.

Robinhood has made its first proprietary Bitcoin purchase, putting approximately $25 million of company money into BTC — crossing a threshold that separates platforms that merely facilitate Bitcoin trading from companies that actually hold it.

Standard Chartered's Global Head of Digital Assets Research, Geoffrey Kendrick, has raised related concerns about the broader corporate treasury trend, warning that "Bitcoin treasuries are adding to Bitcoin buying pressure for now, but we see a risk that this may reverse over time."Neither warning is directed at Robinhood specifically.

Strategy (the company formerly known as MicroStrategy), which holds approximately 848,000 BTC as of early October 2026 — roughly 69% of all Bitcoin owned by listed companies — is a leveraged BTC pure-play; its equity is designed to move with Bitcoin, and shareholders self-select for that risk.
A post circulating on social media before Wednesday's DAS Asia disclosure cited this figure and claimed Robinhood was a massive Bitcoin holder.
Under the old US GAAP model for crypto assets, companies could only write down Bitcoin holdings when prices fell — but could never recognize gains when prices rose.
But both apply with particular force to an operating company that already earns substantially from Bitcoin trading activity.Custody vs.
Robinhood had 27.4 million funded customers and held $307 billion in platform assets as of Q1 2026.

Those $25 billion in crypto assets spread across Robinhood's customer custody wallets belong entirely to Robinhood's customers — Robinhood holds the private keys, but the coins are not on Robinhood's own books.The $25 million corporate BTC purchase is a different category.

The distinction matters for both accounting and risk: customer custody creates zero direct P&L exposure for Robinhood (it earns custody-related revenue from fees and services, not from BTC price movements).
MARA Holdings and other Bitcoin miners hold substantial secondary positions.

Among traditional, non-Bitcoin-native operating companies, Robinhood joins Tesla and Block (the payments company founded by Jack Dorsey) in what analysts describe as symbolic or diversification allocations rather than primary treasury strategies.The corporate treasury trend has also been bolstered by the FASB accounting shift.

Robinhood has taken a direct stake in bitcoin, adding roughly $25 million of the cryptocurrency to its corporate balance sheet and joining a growing list of public companies treating the token as a treasury asset rather than merely a product for customers.
Bitcoin traded near $84,000 at the time of the disclosure, having closed around $85,540 on Oct.
The move marks a shift in tone from the company's posture just under a year ago, when executives had expressed caution about holding volatile crypto assets on the corporate books.
Robinhood has for years facilitated customer trading in digital tokens, but those holdings are segregated from company treasury assets and do not expose the firm to bitcoin's price swings.

He framed the purchase as conviction, not capital reallocation — "it represents how deeply we care about bitcoin and the ecosystem around it" — and was direct about the scale relative to the company: "Robinhood is a massive company at this point, with a market cap in the $100 billion range. So the $25 million worth of bitcoin is not going to change a lot of the current trajectory of the company."The gap between the $25 million purchase and the $100 billion valuation is deliberate. Robinhood had 27.4 million funded customers and held $307 billion in platform assets as of Q1 2026. A $25 million BTC position is 0.025% of its market cap. The posture is.As recently as November 2025, at Robinhood's third-quarter earnings call, incoming CFO Shiv Verma said the company was "still thinking about" the move, weighing the community-alignment benefit against the cost of tying up capital, and raising the question of whether adding Bitcoin to the balance sheet makes any decision for shareholders who can already buy BTC directly through the Robinhood platform. That deliberation about Bitcoin treasury has now closed.What Changed — and Why It Required an Accounting Rule to Change FirstRobinhood did not buy Bitcoin in 2024 or early 2025 even as corporate BTC adoption accelerated around it. The accounting environment is part of the reason. Under the old US GAAP model for crypto assets, companies could only write down Bitcoin holdings when prices fell — but could never recognize gains when prices rose. A corporate Bitcoin position in 2023 created asymmetric accounting punishment: losses hit the income statement, gains were invisible until the asset was sold. That model made holding BTC on an operating company's books artificially punitive.That changed with FASB Accounting Standards Update 2023-08, issued December 13, 2023 and effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2024. Under ASU 2023-08, in-scope crypto assets — Bitcoin included — must be measured at fair value at every reporting date, with gains and losses flowing through net income each quarter. Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), which had already adopted the standard early, described it in its Q1 2025 filing as likely to "have a material impact on our financial results, increase the volatility of our financial results and affect the carrying value of our bitcoin on our balance sheet."The ASU 2023-08 fair-value rule removed the structural disincentive for operating companies to hold BTC. Robinhood's first balance sheet purchase came roughly nine months after the rule took effect for most companies.What a HOOD Shareholder Actually FacesHere is the structural consequence the headline dollar amount does not fully communicate.Robinhood's revenue is already substantially correlated with Bitcoin prices. In Q4 2024, crypto trading accounted for 53% of Robinhood's transaction-based revenue — then fell to 12.88% in Q2 2026 when Bitcoin's price declined. When BTC drops, Robinhood's trading volumes compress and its crypto transaction revenue contracts. This has been true since the company launched crypto trading.What is new is that the $25 million corporate Bitcoin position is now marked to market every quarter under ASU 2023-08. When Bitcoin prices fall, Robinhood's quarterly earnings will now reflect unrealized losses on its corporate BTC holding — in addition to the revenue contraction from lower trading volumes. When prices rise, the reverse applies, but the point stands structurally: HOOD shareholders face Bitcoin price exposure on two separate lines of the income statement simultaneously, and neither exposure hedges the other.This makes Robinhood's position categorically different from both ends of the corporate Bitcoin spectrum. Strategy (the company formerly known as MicroStrategy), which holds approximately 848,000 BTC as of early October 2026 — roughly 69% of all Bitcoin owned by listed companies — is a leveraged BTC pure-play; its equity is designed to move with Bitcoin, and shareholders self-select for that risk. Robinhood sits in a new category: an operating company whose revenue is already Bitcoin-correlated and whose balance sheet is now also Bitcoin-marked-to-market."Cryptocurrencies' high volatility and uncertain regulatory landscape are misaligned with the fundamental goals of treasury management — stability, liquidity, and capital preservation," David Krause, a finance professor at Marquette University, noted in a January 2026 research publication on corporate Bitcoin holdings. Standard Chartered's Global Head of Digital Assets Research, Geoffrey Kendrick, has raised related concerns about the broader corporate treasury trend, warning that "Bitcoin treasuries are adding to Bitcoin buying pressure for now, but we see a risk that this may reverse over time."Neither warning is directed at Robinhood specifically. But both apply with particular force to an operating company that already earns substantially from Bitcoin trading activity.Custody vs. Corporate: Why the Numbers Look ConfusingRobinhood controls approximately $25 billion in crypto assets across approximately 1.7 million wallet addresses on 12 different blockchains. A post circulating on social media before Wednesday's DAS Asia disclosure cited this figure and claimed Robinhood was a massive Bitcoin holder. Those $25 billion in crypto assets spread across Robinhood's customer custody wallets belong entirely to Robinhood's customers — Robinhood holds the private keys, but the coins are not on Robinhood's own books.The $25 million corporate BTC purchase is a different category. It sits on Robinhood's own balance sheet, subject to FASB ASU 2023-08 quarterly fair-value measurement. The distinction matters for both accounting and risk: customer custody creates zero direct P&L exposure for Robinhood (it earns custody-related revenue from fees and services, not from BTC price movements). The corporate position creates direct earnings exposure every quarter.Bitcoin was trading near $83,360 at the time of the DAS Asia disclosure, per CoinDesk market data.Robinhood's Position in the Corporate Bitcoin LandscapeWith the purchase, Robinhood joins a cohort that has expanded dramatically since Strategy made its initial $250 million BTC purchase in August 2020. More than 170 publicly traded companies worldwide now hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets, with combined corporate holdings exceeding 1.2 million BTC — representing more than 6% of Bitcoin's hard-capped supply of 21 million coins.Strategy remains the dominant holder by orders of magnitude. At approximately 848,000 BTC, it accounts for roughly 69% of all corporate-held Bitcoin globally. MARA Holdings and other Bitcoin miners hold substantial secondary positions. Among traditional, non-Bitcoin-native operating companies, Robinhood joins Tesla and Block (the payments company founded by Jack Dorsey) in what analysts describe as symbolic or diversification allocations rather than primary treasury strategies.The corporate treasury trend has also been bolstered by the FASB accounting shift. More than 140 publicly traded companies had adopted Bitcoin treasury positions in the first quarter of 2026 alone, with corporate treasuries collectively adding roughly 62,000 BTC in that quarter.Robinhood has not disclosed a formal BTC accumulation policy, and Kerbrat's language — emphasizing conviction over capital deployment — signals the company is not attempting to replicate Strategy's leveraged, all-in approach.Why Robinhood Chain Makes This More Than SymbolicRobinhood's Bitcoin balance sheet purchase did not arrive in isolation. It follows 98 days after Robinhood Chain — the company's permissionless Ethereum Layer 2 network built on Arbitrum's Orbit stack — went live on mainnet on July 1, 2026. The chain carries chain ID 4663, processes transactions off the Ethereum mainchain in rollup batches before settling back to Ethereum for security, and uses ETH as its native gas token.Since its mainnet debut, Robinhood Chain has added tokenized stock and ETF products (Stock Tokens), a US dollar stablecoin (USDG), and a yield-bearing lending product called Robinhood Earn.

Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), which had already adopted the standard early, described it in its Q1 2025 filing as likely to "have a material impact on our financial results, increase the volatility of our financial results and affect the carrying value of our bitcoin on our balance sheet."The ASU 2023-08 fair-value rule removed the structural disincentive for operating companies to hold BTC.

When prices rise, the reverse applies, but the point stands structurally: HOOD shareholders face Bitcoin price exposure on two separate lines of the income statement simultaneously, and neither exposure hedges the other.This makes Robinhood's position categorically different from both ends of the corporate Bitcoin spectrum.
In Q4 2024, crypto trading accounted for 53% of Robinhood's transaction-based revenue — then fell to 12.88% in Q2 2026 when Bitcoin's price declined.

Robinhood has made its first proprietary Bitcoin purchase, putting approximately $25 million of company money into BTC — crossing a threshold that separates platforms that merely facilitate Bitcoin trading from companies that actually hold it.

Standard Chartered's Global Head of Digital Assets Research, Geoffrey Kendrick, has raised related concerns about the broader corporate treasury trend, warning that "Bitcoin treasuries are adding to Bitcoin buying pressure for now, but we see a risk that this may reverse over time."Neither warning is directed at Robinhood specifically.

Strategy (the company formerly known as MicroStrategy), which holds approximately 848,000 BTC as of early October 2026 — roughly 69% of all Bitcoin owned by listed companies — is a leveraged BTC pure-play; its equity is designed to move with Bitcoin, and shareholders self-select for that risk.
A post circulating on social media before Wednesday's DAS Asia disclosure cited this figure and claimed Robinhood was a massive Bitcoin holder.
Under the old US GAAP model for crypto assets, companies could only write down Bitcoin holdings when prices fell — but could never recognize gains when prices rose.
But both apply with particular force to an operating company that already earns substantially from Bitcoin trading activity.Custody vs.
Robinhood had 27.4 million funded customers and held $307 billion in platform assets as of Q1 2026.

Those $25 billion in crypto assets spread across Robinhood's customer custody wallets belong entirely to Robinhood's customers — Robinhood holds the private keys, but the coins are not on Robinhood's own books.The $25 million corporate BTC purchase is a different category.

The distinction matters for both accounting and risk: customer custody creates zero direct P&L exposure for Robinhood (it earns custody-related revenue from fees and services, not from BTC price movements).
MARA Holdings and other Bitcoin miners hold substantial secondary positions.

Among traditional, non-Bitcoin-native operating companies, Robinhood joins Tesla and Block (the payments company founded by Jack Dorsey) in what analysts describe as symbolic or diversification allocations rather than primary treasury strategies.The corporate treasury trend has also been bolstered by the FASB accounting shift.

extraction.body: Robinhood has taken a direct stake in bitcoin, adding roughly $25 million of the cryptocurrency to its corporate balance sheet and joining a growing list of public companies treating the token as a treasury asset rather than merely a product for customers. The purchase was disclosed Wednesday by Johann Kerbrat, Robinhood's senior vice president and general manager of crypto and international, during an interview with The Block's Starting Block program at the Digital Asset Summit Asia conference in Singapore. The company has not separately confirmed the transaction through a press release or regulatory filing. "We care deeply about bitcoin and the ecosystem around it," Kerbrat said. "For us, it's more aligning our company and our vision with the crypto community." The executive was careful to frame the allocation as a strategic signal rather than a financial bet that would reshape the company's trajectory. With Robinhood's market capitalization hovering around $100 billion, he noted, a $25 million bitcoin position "is not going to change a lot of the current trajectory of the company." The move marks a shift in tone from the company's posture just under a year ago, when executives had expressed caution about holding volatile crypto assets on the corporate books. Robinhood has for years facilitated customer trading in digital tokens, but those holdings are segregated from company treasury assets and do not expose the firm to bitcoin's price swings. The new allocation changes that dynamic, giving Robinhood direct exposure to the cryptocurrency's market value. Robinhood now stands alongside more than 170 publicly traded companies worldwide that hold bitcoin as a corporate asset, a trend that Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR) initiated in 2020 when it began converting cash reserves into the cryptocurrency. Current corporate holders include Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA), Block (NYSE:XYZ), MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA), CleanSpark (NASDAQ:CLSK) and Riot Platforms (NASDAQ:RIOT). Together, those firms and others account for well over 1.2 million bitcoin on their balance sheets. Strategy continues to add to its position. The company disclosed this week that it purchased an additional 334 bitcoin between Sept. 28 and Oct. 4 for roughly $28.7 million, at an average price of $85,838.80 per coin. That brings its total holdings to 848,000 bitcoin, far eclipsing any other corporate treasury. Robinhood's $25 million allocation is modest by comparison, but it carries outsized symbolic weight given the brokerage's visibility among retail investors and its more than 28 million funded customers globally. The company has been methodically expanding its crypto footprint beyond simple spot trading. In July, it launched Robinhood Chain, an Ethereum-compatible Layer 2 network built on Arbitrum and designed for tokenized real-world assets and decentralized finance. Since the mainnet went live, the chain has rolled out tokenized stock products, a stablecoin called USDG, and yield-bearing lending through Robinhood Earn, while integrating DeFi protocols such as Uniswap and infrastructure from Chainlink, Alchemy and BitGo. The network has already reached $1.05 billion in total value locked, according to earlier reporting. Kerbrat said trading volume for stock tokens on the chain has grown to the point where it is approaching limits set by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's innovation exemption for tokenized U.S. equities. Robinhood has also signaled plans to launch perpetual futures trading for eligible U.S. customers, covering eight assets. Chief Executive Officer Vlad Tenev has described the offering as "America's first true perps," with no expiry and profit and loss settled every 15 minutes. The company reported 28.6 million funded customers and $384 billion in total platform assets for August. Crypto notional trading volume reached $17.5 billion during that month, underscoring why the bitcoin treasury position is viewed more as an alignment of corporate identity with the asset class than as a meaningful capital allocation. Bitcoin traded near $84,000 at the time of the disclosure, having closed around $85,540 on Oct. 6. The cryptocurrency has remained below recent local highs, and a $25 million purchase is unlikely to move its price in any meaningful way given the asset's overall market size. Robinhood shares were down roughly 3% in premarket trading, extending a pullback from a recent high of $125. The stock has broken below its 20-day exponential moving average at $114 and is testing the 50-day exponential moving average near $109, with the relative strength index at 48.75 indicating fading momentum. The shares still hold above the 100-day and 200-day exponential moving averages, suggesting the longer-term uptrend remains intact. For investors, the more significant implication lies in signaling. A consumer-facing brokerage with millions of users formalizing a direct bitcoin position reinforces the narrative that the cryptocurrency is becoming a standard corporate treasury consideration, particularly for companies with crypto-adjacent business lines. It also invites scrutiny of how such holdings will be valued and disclosed in future financial reporting. Robinhood has not detailed a long-term target size for its bitcoin holdings, nor has it indicated whether additional allocations or other digital assets might follow. The company's press team did not immediately respond to inquiries about potential future purchases. The disclosure arrives amid continued competition among brokerages, exchanges and fintech platforms to capture crypto-focused customers. Firms are increasingly differentiating themselves not just through trading fees, but through the depth of their underlying commitment to digital assets. Robinhood's balance sheet purchase adds another data point to that competitive landscape, one that suggests the company sees its own treasury as another venue for demonstrating conviction in the asset class it increasingly serves. For 2026, Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (GOOGL) now projects that it will lay out between $175 billion and $185 billion on capital expenditures -- nearly double the amount it spent on them in 2025. That massive budget, which will largely go toward data centers, networking equipment, AI processors, and servers, is meant to keep the tech giant at the front of the pack in the increasingly expensive artificial intelligence (AI) race. Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue » But is this extensive infrastructure buildout a strategic masterstroke or a big mistake? The tech world is full of examples of companies that don't adapt to innovation quickly enough. Kodak had the chance to get into digital cameras early, but failed to. BlackBerry dismissed touchscreens. Blockbuster didn't take video streaming seriously. Executives are well aware of those history lessons and want to avoid having their businesses become case studies of what happens when a company doesn't adjust in time. If the value that AI winds up delivering lives up to the hype, Alphabet will have a solid foothold in that market that it will be able to enhance as it makes more investments. It has the chips and cloud services other companies need for the AI buildout, with its cloud division in particular offering a bright spot. In Q4 2025, Google Cloud revenue increased 48% year over year to $17.6 billion, and the segment's operating income increased 30.1% to $5.3 billion. Another proof point for Alphabet's cloud strength for AI use can be found in its backlog. "Google Cloud's backlog increased 55% sequentially and more than doubled year over year, reaching $240 billion at the end of the fourth quarter," said CFO Anat Ashkenazi on the company's Q4 earnings call. "The increase in backlog was driven by strong demand for our cloud products, led by our enterprise AI offerings, from multiple customers." It also has its own in-house products that it can optimize and monetize using AI, such as Google Search . Whenever you invest in a company, it's exciting to think about what can go right, but what's equally important, if not more so, is considering what can go wrong. There are several risks that come with Alphabet's impressive spending plans. One is that Wall Street may not have the patience to let the narrative fully play out before reaching a verdict on the stock. For example, Alphabet delivered what was generally considered a strong Q4 report, beating consensus top and bottom-line expectations. The stock price still took a hit, however, as management announced the scale of its 2026 capital expenditure plans. On Feb. 4, the day of the earnings announcement, Alphabet's Class A shares opened at $342.96. The next day, they opened 9% lower at at $312.09. That shows how much short-term concern can weigh down the stock price, but the biggest risk for the tech giant is that demand for AI processing power might not live up to expectations in the long term. If AI demand isn't at the levels expected for all the big tech players building out the infrastructure, the fears that they have been overspending could prove prophetic. As one of the companies with one of the biggest spending plans, Alphabet could be hit especially hard. Since the AI race started, Alphabet has been in a precarious position. One of the narratives early in the AI race was that Alphabet was caught flat-footed by OpenAI's launch of ChatGPT. Alphabet shifted that perception last year, and its shares rebounded, climbing roughly 66%. For 2026, one predominant theme in the market is worry that tech giants are spending too much on AI infrastructure when they may not reap strong enough returns on those investments. To separate the noise from what matters in this case, it helps to consider Alphabet's financial situation. It isn't a risky start-up going all-in on a speculative technology that will either make it or break it. It's generating huge profits in the here and now, with net income of $132 billion in 2025, a 32% increase from 2024. It also has diverse revenue sources and a bankroll that should allow it to navigate any setbacks and stumbles it encounters. Overall, whether you believe Alphabet needs to ramp up its spending or cut back on it, this will still require more than a quarter-to-quarter mindset as we all watch to see how it plays out. For 2026, Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (GOOGL) now projects that it will lay out between $175 billion and $185 billion on capital expenditures -- nearly double the amount it spent on them in 2025. That massive budget, which will largely go toward data centers, networking equipment, AI processors, and servers, is meant to keep the tech giant at the front of the pack in the increasingly expensive artificial intelligence (AI) race. Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue » But is this extensive infrastructure buildout a strategic masterstroke or a big mistake? The tech world is full of examples of companies that don't adapt to innovation quickly enough. Kodak had the chance to get into digital cameras early, but failed to. BlackBerry dismissed touchscreens. Blockbuster didn't take video streaming seriously. Executives are well aware of those history lessons and want to avoid having their businesses become case studies of what happens when a company doesn't adjust in time. If the value that AI winds up delivering lives up to the hype, Alphabet will have a solid foothold in that market that it will be able to enhance as it makes more investments. It has the chips and cloud services other companies need for the AI buildout, with its cloud division in particular offering a bright spot. In Q4 2025, Google Cloud revenue increased 48% year over year to $17.6 billion, and the segment's operating income increased 30.1% to $5.3 billion. Another proof point for Alphabet's cloud strength for AI use can be found in its backlog. "Google Cloud's backlog increased 55% sequentially and more than doubled year over year, reaching $240 billion at the end of the fourth quarter," said CFO Anat Ashkenazi on the company's Q4 earnings call. "The increase in backlog was driven by strong demand for our cloud products, led by our enterprise AI offerings, from multiple customers." It also has its own in-house products that it can optimize and monetize using AI, such as Google Search . Whenever you invest in a company, it's exciting to think about what can go right, but what's equally important, if not more so, is considering what can go wrong. There are several risks that come with Alphabet's impressive spending plans. One is that Wall Street may not have the patience to let the narrative fully play out before reaching a verdict on the stock. For example, Alphabet delivered what was generally considered a strong Q4 report, beating consensus top and bottom-line expectations. The stock price still took a hit, however, as management announced the scale of its 2026 capital expenditure plans. On Feb. 4, the day of the earnings announcement, Alphabet's Class A shares opened at $342.96. The next day, they opened 9% lower at at $312.09. That shows how much short-term concern can weigh down the stock price, but the biggest risk for the tech giant is that demand for AI processing power might not live up to expectations in the long term. If AI demand isn't at the levels expected for all the big tech players building out the infrastructure, the fears that they have been overspending could prove prophetic. As one of the companies with one of the biggest spending plans, Alphabet could be hit especially hard. Since the AI race started, Alphabet has been in a precarious position. One of the narratives early in the AI race was that Alphabet was caught flat-footed by OpenAI's launch of ChatGPT. Alphabet shifted that perception last year, and its shares rebounded, climbing roughly 66%. For 2026, one predominant theme in the market is worry that tech giants are spending too much on AI infrastructure when they may not reap strong enough returns on those investments. To separate the noise from what matters in this case, it helps to consider Alphabet's financial situation. It isn't a risky start-up going all-in on a speculative technology that will either make it or break it. It's generating huge profits in the here and now, with net income of $132 billion in 2025, a 32% increase from 2024. It also has diverse revenue sources and a bankroll that should allow it to navigate any setbacks and stumbles it encounters. Overall, whether you believe Alphabet needs to ramp up its spending or cut back on it, this will still require more than a quarter-to-quarter mindset as we all watch to see how it plays out. sources.title: ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface
passages: ChatGPT is about to get a lot more visual, thanks to a new feature that OpenAI calls Intelligent UI.
The new interface, which is being rolled out Wednesday with a new GPT-6 model, will integrate a significant amount of visuals into users’ conversations.

Aarush Selvan, a product manager at the company, said that while “ChatGPT has predominantly been a text-based interface,” the company really wants to help users “get things done — from everyday things like planning a recipe or a trip or even trying to learn something — the most helpful answers aren’t just text.”
Selvan gave the example of a college student wanting to know how an airplane wing functions.
As with other aspects of ChatGPT’s personality, if users don’t want so many visuals in their responses, they’ll be able to dial them back.
Intelligent UI rolls out globally with GPT-6 for Pro, Plus, Business, and Enterprise users, and arrives Thursday for users of the free and lower-cost Go tiers.

The big goal here, according to OpenAI, is to make “learning complex topics easier.” It may also make ChatGPT friendlier and more accessible and help bring in a wider audience, though OpenAI didn’t say so directly.

extraction.body: ChatGPT is about to get a lot more visual, thanks to a new feature that OpenAI calls Intelligent UI. The new interface, which is being rolled out Wednesday with a new GPT-6 model, will integrate a significant amount of visuals into users’ conversations. OpenAI says many of those visuals will be interactive. In other words, instead of just flat, cartoonish pictures, the chatbot will frequently include things like tappable buttons, a customized calculator for a specific task, interactive charts, editable graphs, and other elements the user can work with directly. The big goal here, according to OpenAI, is to make “learning complex topics easier.” It may also make ChatGPT friendlier and more accessible and help bring in a wider audience, though OpenAI didn’t say so directly. In a call with journalists, OpenAI staff gave a brief demonstration of Intelligent UI’s capabilities, showing how the new chatbot can instantly whip up various diagrams and visuals that help users understand more abstract topics. Aarush Selvan, a product manager at the company, said that while “ChatGPT has predominantly been a text-based interface,” the company really wants to help users “get things done — from everyday things like planning a recipe or a trip or even trying to learn something — the most helpful answers aren’t just text.” Selvan gave the example of a college student wanting to know how an airplane wing functions. He asked ChatGPT to “explore how an airplane wing generates lift” and the chatbot quickly spun up a number of diagrams designed to show how planes stay in the air. Other examples from the company included things like visuals for recipes, a diagram explaining bicycle mechanics, a map for a multi-day hiking excursion, a personal savings calculator, and more. This new feature will be customizable. As with other aspects of ChatGPT’s personality, if users don’t want so many visuals in their responses, they’ll be able to dial them back. Intelligent UI rolls out globally with GPT-6 for Pro, Plus, Business, and Enterprise users, and arrives Thursday for users of the free and lower-cost Go tiers. OpenAI is rolling out a new user interface that adds interactive visuals to ChatGPT, and it wants you to stop reading explanations and start playing with them. 
 The feature, called dynamic visual explanations , was announced on March 10, 2026. It lets users manipulate math and science concepts directly instead of scrolling through another wall of text. 
 

 How dynamic visual explanations work 
 The core idea is simple. Instead of describing how a concept behaves, ChatGPT now shows it, and then hands you the controls. 
 OpenAI’s own example is the Pythagorean theorem. Users can adjust the sides of a triangle and watch the result change instantly as they move things around.

The current lineup of 70-plus topics is a starting point, not the finished catalog. When ChatGPT first launched in 2022, the experience was almost entirely text. You typed a question, and the model typed back. In late 2024, the company introduced Canvas, a workspace that let users create and work with content alongside the model. Then in October 2025, OpenAI brought interactive third-party applications into the platform. That move opened the door for outside tools to operate inside ChatGPT itself. Dynamic visual explanations fit neatly into that progression. Canvas gave users a place to build. Third-party apps gave them more tools. Now, ChatGPT is generating interactive learning material on its own. The most immediate stakeholders are students and teachers. With the feature available to all logged-in users, the barrier to trying it is low, and the 70-plus supported topics cover a lot of core curriculum territory. The expansion roadmap is the other variable. OpenAI has said it will add more interactive modules over time, but the pace and breadth of that expansion will determine whether dynamic visual explanations become a core part of ChatGPT or remain a niche study aid. sources.title: OpenAI Launches Visual Ads in ChatGPT with New Measurement Tools
passages: OpenAI has quietly launched a sophisticated visual ad format within ChatGPT, complete with expanded measurement tools and attribution partnerships that could fundamentally change how brands reach consumers in the age of conversational AI.

Unlike traditional search or social media advertising, these new visual ads integrate directly into AI conversations, creating what industry insiders are calling "contextual advertising 2.0." What makes this launch particularly significant is OpenAI's approach to measurement and attribution.
With ChatGPT now processing over 100 million weekly active users, OpenAI is sitting on one of the most engaged digital audiences in history.
The measurement tools represent perhaps the most sophisticated attribution system ever built for conversational interfaces.

OpenAI's move into visual advertising represents more than just a new revenue stream - it's a fundamental shift in how AI companies will sustain their massive operational costs while scaling globally.
Rather than interrupting conversations with jarring display ads, OpenAI's visual format seems designed to integrate seamlessly into the chat experience.

What makes this launch particularly significant is OpenAI's approach to measurement and attribution. The company isn't just throwing ads into chat windows and hoping for the best. According to the announcement, they're building comprehensive tracking capabilities that let advertisers understand how AI-powered conversations actually drive purchasing decisions. This represents a massive departure from OpenAI's subscription-only revenue model. What's particularly interesting is how this positions OpenAI against other AI companies. While Anthropic and others have focused purely on AI safety and capabilities, OpenAI is aggressively building the commercial infrastructure needed to sustain long-term development. The implications extend far beyond OpenAI itself. Every major tech company is now racing to integrate conversational AI into their products. Microsoft with Copilot, Google with Bard, and Meta with various AI initiatives all need sustainable monetization strategies. OpenAI's move into visual advertising represents more than just a new revenue stream - it's a fundamental shift in how AI companies will sustain their massive operational costs while scaling globally. As conversational AI becomes the primary interface between humans and digital services, traditional advertising models will need complete reinvention.

coreStoryFacts.text: ChatGPT is about to get a lot more visual, thanks to a new feature that OpenAI calls Intelligent UI.
The new interface, which is being rolled out Wednesday with a new GPT-6 model, will integrate a significant amount of visuals into users’ conversations.

Aarush Selvan, a product manager at the company, said that while “ChatGPT has predominantly been a text-based interface,” the company really wants to help users “get things done — from everyday things like planning a recipe or a trip or even trying to learn something — the most helpful answers aren’t just text.”
Selvan gave the example of a college student wanting to know how an airplane wing functions.
As with other aspects of ChatGPT’s personality, if users don’t want so many visuals in their responses, they’ll be able to dial them back.
Intelligent UI rolls out globally with GPT-6 for Pro, Plus, Business, and Enterprise users, and arrives Thursday for users of the free and lower-cost Go tiers.

The big goal here, according to OpenAI, is to make “learning complex topics easier.” It may also make ChatGPT friendlier and more accessible and help bring in a wider audience, though OpenAI didn’t say so directly.

extraction.body: ChatGPT is about to get a lot more visual, thanks to a new feature that OpenAI calls Intelligent UI. The new interface, which is being rolled out Wednesday with a new GPT-6 model, will integrate a significant amount of visuals into users’ conversations. OpenAI says many of those visuals will be interactive. In other words, instead of just flat, cartoonish pictures, the chatbot will frequently include things like tappable buttons, a customized calculator for a specific task, interactive charts, editable graphs, and other elements the user can work with directly. The big goal here, according to OpenAI, is to make “learning complex topics easier.” It may also make ChatGPT friendlier and more accessible and help bring in a wider audience, though OpenAI didn’t say so directly. In a call with journalists, OpenAI staff gave a brief demonstration of Intelligent UI’s capabilities, showing how the new chatbot can instantly whip up various diagrams and visuals that help users understand more abstract topics. Aarush Selvan, a product manager at the company, said that while “ChatGPT has predominantly been a text-based interface,” the company really wants to help users “get things done — from everyday things like planning a recipe or a trip or even trying to learn something — the most helpful answers aren’t just text.” Selvan gave the example of a college student wanting to know how an airplane wing functions. He asked ChatGPT to “explore how an airplane wing generates lift” and the chatbot quickly spun up a number of diagrams designed to show how planes stay in the air. sources.title: OpenAI Launches Visual Ads in ChatGPT with New Measurement Tools
passages: OpenAI has quietly launched a sophisticated visual ad format within ChatGPT, complete with expanded measurement tools and attribution partnerships that could fundamentally change how brands reach consumers in the age of conversational AI.

Unlike traditional search or social media advertising, these new visual ads integrate directly into AI conversations, creating what industry insiders are calling "contextual advertising 2.0." What makes this launch particularly significant is OpenAI's approach to measurement and attribution.
With ChatGPT now processing over 100 million weekly active users, OpenAI is sitting on one of the most engaged digital audiences in history.
The measurement tools represent perhaps the most sophisticated attribution system ever built for conversational interfaces.

OpenAI's move into visual advertising represents more than just a new revenue stream - it's a fundamental shift in how AI companies will sustain their massive operational costs while scaling globally.
Rather than interrupting conversations with jarring display ads, OpenAI's visual format seems designed to integrate seamlessly into the chat experience.

While Anthropic and others have focused purely on AI safety and capabilities, OpenAI is aggressively building the commercial infrastructure needed to sustain long-term development. Embiricos leads the Dots product and brings some relevant history to the role. He co-founded Multi, a collaboration tool that OpenAI acquired in June 2024. extraction.body: Teenage Engineering founder and CEO Jesper Kouthoofd told Highsnobiety that it plans to stop making synths. And yes, that includes the iconic OP-1, which put the company on the map. But almost everything the company makes itself — the OP-1, the OP-XY, EP-133, TP-7, et cetera — is music or audio-focused. sources.title: Teenage Engineering’s OP-1 Instrument: Hands-on, Videos, Why it’s Different - CDM Create Digital Music
passages: Teenage Engineering’s OP-1 is something unique in music hardware.
It’s got a form factor inspired by the Casio VL-Tone series – you know, those cute little 80s-vintage synths .
It has, we’ve just learned, a multi-track tape mode that lets you do beat-synced virtual splicing as a performance technique.

It is expected to integrate and interoperate with a design lifestyle including, if you like, a luxury-priced, meticulously-machined desk lamp, and according to one rumor I heard, perhaps even a specially-designed electric bicycle. (Seriously.)

I do mean “the guys” – I had expected to go out to dinner with the CEO and found myself with almost the entire team of 9. (One was sleeping off Sweden-to-California jetlag.) The company has a pedigree in sound engineering, including the legendary drum maker Elektron, but also in marketing, advertising, industrial and product design.
The screen isn’t just beautiful: it fits perfectly.
Since computers became commonplace in the 80s, the primitive screens on music hardware have seemed an anachronism, a compromise.
I remember synth shopping for the first time around 1990 and being frustrated by that, and things aren’t much different now.
The display itself seems like part of the hardware and the instrument, rather than being a menu system or a tacked-on indicator.
The craft of early electronic music was deeply connected to the process of recording to tape, then splicing, into a finished product as a collage.
A simple, iconic on-screen representation of a reel-to-reel shows you your recording in real-time, with even some light physics simulation so it behaves like tape when you stop the transport.
But you can also cut the virtual tape – split, lift and join features are quick key shortcuts away.
Just like on tape, you can change the speed during recording, not just during playback .
And, so as not to be too caught in the past, the tape deck itself can be beat-synced .
Let’s just reflect on that for a second: you can sample the instrument or an external source, and then speed and slow the recording like tape synced to beat, all on hardware.
Sampling features are nothing new, but the implementation here really is something special.
Watch it in action in this video of a live jam, shot by Teenage Engineering and smuggled off one of their computers for CDM :
The synth and sampler are friendly – toy-like in the best way.
Color-coded knobs and extensive graphical feedback make a reasonably sophisticated set of synthesis, envelope, and sampling options accessible.
Pricing will be under US$1000 – perhaps a goodly amount under, depending on the final details of manufacturing.
There’s no availability date, but progress appears to be accelerating.
I poked fun when the OP-1 was introduced, only because it seems like something too cool to be real.
Some of the little touches I was able to glean:
Go crazy with this, and you can prove some pretty out-there results.
